subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should OpenClaw broaden macOS updater cleanup to all observed OpenClaw update job families and make same-version package updates no-op before managed-service stop/restart, or wait for a fresh current-main macOS smoke to narrow the fix?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent launchd label ownership and same-version update behavior are product/lifecycle policy choices with upgrade impact.

options.title: Broaden cleanup and no-op policy
options.body: Treat `manualupdate`, legacy `manual-update-*`, and `oob-update` families as stale OpenClaw updater jobs, skip same-version service stop/restart work, and require macOS launchd proof before close.

options.title: Split the cluster first
options.body: Keep this issue canonical while splitting service bootstrap recovery, node-host skew, and stale updater cleanup into narrower owner-reviewed issues.

options.title: Wait for current-main live repro
options.body: Hold implementation until a current-main macOS smoke reproduces the loop and identifies the smallest failing updater path.

recommendation.title: Broaden cleanup and no-op policy
recommendation.body: Treat `manualupdate`, legacy `manual-update-*`, and `oob-update` families as stale OpenClaw updater jobs, skip same-version service stop/restart work, and require macOS launchd proof before close.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent macOS package service and update lifecycle work is closest to the policy boundary and launchd recovery behavior.
